Where $\mu_{1:3}$ is the spatial part of the mean, $\Sigma_{1:3,4}$ is the cross-covariance between space and time, and $\Sigma_{4,4}$ is the temporal variance [S4, unofficial].

The claim states that $mu_{1:3}$ is the spatial part of the mean, $Sigma_{1:3,4}$ is the cross-covariance between space and time, and $Sigma_{4,4}$ is the temporal variance. The provided evidence explicitly defines the 4D mean as $mu = (mu_x, mu_y, mu_z, mu_t)$, implying $mu_{1:3}$ corresponds to the spatial components $(mu_x, mu_y, mu_z)$. It further provides the equation for the conditional mean $mu_{xyz|t} = mu_{1:3} + Sigma_{1:3,4} Sigma_{4,4}^{-1} (t - mu_t)$, which is the standard formula for conditional Gaussian distributions where $Sigma_{1:3,4}$ represents the covariance between the spatial variables (1-3) and the temporal variable (4). Finally, it defines the marginal time probability $p(t) = N(t; mu_4, Sigma_{4,4})$, identifying $Sigma_{4,4}$ as the variance of the time dimension. Thus, all facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
